name: Aveiro
title: Holidays in Aveiro
intro: Portugal's little Venice, with colourful boats on canals, art nouveau houses, striped beach cottages and sweet egg pastries. Here's what Aveiro is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Brightly painted moliceiro boats moored on a canal in Aveiro
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April to June and September to October are best, mild for walking and boat rides. July and August are warm with busy beaches. Winter is cool and rainy.

things.name: Moliceiro boat ride
things.blurb: A trip along the canals on a painted former seaweed boat.

things.name: Costa Nova
things.blurb: Candy-striped beach houses and a long Atlantic beach, 15 minutes away.

things.name: Ovos moles
things.blurb: Sweet egg-yolk sweets in wafer shells shaped like fish and shells.

things.name: Art nouveau museum
things.blurb: A small museum and tea room in one of the town's art nouveau houses.

things.name: Salt pans
things.blurb: Learn how salt is made, and float in salty pools.

faqs.question: Is Aveiro worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a day or two. The canals, painted boats and striped houses at Costa Nova are charming.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Aveiro?
faqs.answer: One or two days covers the town and Costa Nova.

faqs.question: How do you get to Aveiro?
faqs.answer: Fly into Porto, which has direct flights from the UK, then take the train, about 40 minutes to an hour.

faqs.question: Can you visit Aveiro as a day trip from Porto?
faqs.answer: Yes. Trains run often, and many tours combine Aveiro and Costa Nova.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Aveiro?
faqs.answer: April to June and September, around 18 to 24°C.
